chunks: Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

"Whoever intentionally eats saffron or food containing fragrance, then a blood sacrifice is upon him. But if he was forgetful, then there is nothing upon him, and he should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him."

key_terms.دَمٌ: a blood sacrifice; expiatory animal offering
key_terms.زَعْفَرَانًا: saffron, specifically as a scented substance prohibited here in the state of ihram
key_terms.طِيبٌ: fragrance or perfume present in food
key_terms.يَتُوبُ: he repents and returns to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a muhrim who intentionally or forgetfully eats saffron or fragrant food?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the muhrim: intentionally consuming saffron or fragrant food entails a dam. If it occurs out of forgetfulness, no expiation is due, though one should seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.
